result: In a pilot of 11 ME/CFS+FM, 11 ME/CFS-FM and 11 controls (33 natural autoantibodies by ELISA), both patient groups showed more frequent deviations in GABA-receptor immunoreactivity, other levels did not differ, and autoantibody correlation patterns with fatigue, pain and mood differed from controls.
reason: Measures neural-antigen autoantibodies (GABA receptors), not beta2/muscarinic GPCR IgG; fits the neural-autoantibody finding with mixed symptom associations.

result: In 200 ME/CFS vs 150 controls by PCR, active HHV-6A/B, HHV-7 and/or B19V infection was found in 45% vs 8.7%, with higher viral loads and higher TNF-alpha, IL-12 and IL-10 in active infection and in severe vs moderate disease.
reason: Does not test inherited chromosomally integrated HHV-6; reports more active persistent herpes/B19 infection in blood, which conflicts with the blood-virome null and bears on parvovirus B19.

result: Of 34 non-hospitalised PASC patients who met ME/CFS criteria at baseline on the DSQ, fatigue, PEM, brain fog, IBS symptoms and unsteadiness improved significantly over 1 year and improvers no longer met criteria, while 151 ME/CFS patients showed no improvement.
reason: Same question (course of post-COVID patients meeting ME/CFS criteria) but finds improvement, against the Charité persistence result; small sample.

result: In 49 ME/CFS vs 10 sedentary controls across a 2-day CPET, at most two symptom types (fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, low mood, decreased function) discriminated groups at each of five timepoints, and one symptom sufficed at one week after the second test.
reason: Builds a symptom-based PEM detection rule; does not measure PEM onset delay or recovery duration, and no atlas finding covers PEM screening instruments.

result: On 24-h Holter in 47 long COVID patients vs 42 controls, SDNN24, SDANNI and HF power were lower and LF higher in long COVID, alongside raised CNP, D-dimer and CRP.
reason: Same measure and direction (lower HF-HRV) but in long COVID, not an independent ME/CFS cohort, so extends rather than replicates.

result: Of 465 mainly white, female, North American long COVID respondents (mean 70.5 weeks after onset), 58% met an ME/CFS case definition by validated short-form questionnaire, with both over- and under-self-diagnosis.
reason: Reports the proportion of long COVID meeting ME/CFS criteria, in line with the 51% meta-analytic figure; self-selected survey without uninfected comparison.

result: In 42 ME/CFS (18 ICC, 24 Fukuda) vs 24 controls, only two resting-state salience-network connections differed (Fukuda only), while task fMRI showed 10 differing connections (5 ICC, 5 Fukuda, none shared), including stronger salience-hippocampus and salience-brainstem RAS connectivity.
reason: Same measure (salience/DMN/brainstem connectivity) and adds a diagnostic-criteria subgroup split; sparse resting differences fit the contested grade. Check whether this is the cited Barnden 2023 (author not in abstract).

result: In 29 people with post-COVID symptoms vs 20 recovered COVID controls, fatigue (FAS, FSS), pain and quality of life were worse, but isokinetic torque and work fatigue indices did not differ (all p >= 0.07).
reason: No brain-activity measure; it tests objective muscle fatigability, closest to the repeated-strength fatigability finding, and finds no difference in long COVID.

result: By Simoa, plasma NfL was raised in 102 hospitalised COVID-19 patients vs 96 matched controls and rose further during admission, but after age adjustment neither NfL nor p-tau181 was elevated in 119 PASC outpatients with or without brain fog.
reason: Same markers and method, null result in long COVID consistent with the ME/CFS null; extends to PASC.

result: UK/Ireland paediatric surveillance found 33 severe, 4 probable and 55 possible severe ME/CFS cases aged 5-16, a prevalence of 3.2 per million (8.9 including possible/probable) and incidence of 0.90 per million child-years, median age 13, 58% female.
reason: Measures population prevalence of severe paediatric ME/CFS, not the share of patients who are housebound or severity as a treatment-response predictor; no atlas finding covers it (could be screened as new epidemiology).
